permutationLabel: Late: transmural infarction with septic shock
summary: 71-year-old man with un-anticoagulated AF and PAD, 30 h after sudden pain: peritonitis, PR blood, T 38.4 °C, HR 134, BP 84/52, lactate 6.8; CTA: SMA occlusion with pneumatosis and portal venous gas.

inputs.hpi: 30 hours of severe central abdominal pain after sudden onset; initially the GP found a soft abdomen. Now distended, vomiting, dark blood per rectum, collapsed at home. Atrial fibrillation, never anticoagulated. Peripheral arterial disease.

exam.general: Drowsy, mottled. Temperature 38.4°C, pulse 134/min irregular, BP 84/52, RR 30.
exam.abdomen: Distended, generalised peritonitis with rigidity. Dark blood on PR.

imaging.name: CT angiography abdomen
imaging.result: Occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery 3 cm from its origin with no distal filling; small-bowel pneumatosis, portal venous gas and free fluid — transmural infarction.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute mesenteric ischaemia with bowel infarction
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute arterial mesenteric ischaemia (SMA embolus) with transmural small-bowel infarction and septic shock. Resuscitation, heparin, emergency laparotomy with revascularisation and resection of non-viable bowel; damage control and second look.

socratesAnswers.associated: Vomiting, dark blood per rectum, fever, collapse

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no acute mesenteric ischaemia disease node, so it can never appear in the PANE top 3 (inguinal/femoral hernia, cholecystitis, cholangitis).

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Abdominal pain and collapse' gives 'routine'.

mustInclude.note: Revascularisation of the SMA before or with resection improves survival.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No revascularisation step; only laparotomy/resection templates.
mustInclude.proposedFix: As above: AMI protocol with revascularisation before/with resection.

guideline.name: ESVS clinical practice guidelines — diseases of the mesenteric arteries and veins
guideline.section: Acute mesenteric ischaemia: suspicion (pain out of proportion, AF), lactate not sensitive/specific enough to exclude, immediate CT angiography, heparin, revascularisation, resection of non-viable bowel; mesenteric venous thrombosis: anticoagulation
guideline.citation: Björck M, Koelemay M, Acosta S, et al. Management of the diseases of mesenteric arteries and veins: clinical practice guidelines of the European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS). Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2017;53:460–510.

guideline.name: WSES updated guidelines — acute mesenteric ischaemia
guideline.section: High index of suspicion; normal lactate does not exclude AMI; CT angiography without delay; systemic anticoagulation; revascularisation; damage control / second look; antibiotics
guideline.citation: Bala M, Catena F, Kashuk J, et al. Acute mesenteric ischemia: updated guidelines of the World Society of Emergency Surgery. World J Emerg Surg. 2022;17:54.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — international guidelines for sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening (do not use qSOFA alone), antibiotics within 1 h of shock, blood cultures, lactate, 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypoperfusion, vasopressors, source control
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: late presentation. Tests shock/sepsis alarms and a plan that combines emergency laparotomy with revascularisation, damage control and second look.
